example_models.translation: I know that the fish is good.
example_models.note: Known fact; indicative is, with gōd agreeing with masculine fisc.

example_models.translation: He says that the fish is good.
example_models.note: Reported assertion; selected present subjunctive sīe does not add an English wish meaning.

example_models.translation: He said that the fish was good.
example_models.note: Reported state at the time of past speech; wǣre is the selected preterite subjunctive.
Hwæt is the embedded object's accusative; the matrix knowing frame does not determine its case.

example_models.translation: Tell me whether the men are ready.
example_models.note: Mē is the dative recipient of the request; whether is invariant and the embedded subject is plural.

example_models.translation: The man commanded him to carry the fish.
example_models.note: The commanded actor is hine; the fish is the separate object of carrying.

example_models.translation: I see the man carrying the fish.
example_models.note: The perceived actor is the accusative man, and the infinitive keeps its accusative fish object.
Gōdne is the strong accusative predicate adjective agreeing with the object.
A present unreal wish in the stated context, not an assertion about a past reign.

example_models.translation: I want/am willing to carry the fish.
example_models.note: The matrix subject is also the understood actor of the plain infinitive.
Cyning is a noun predicate in the prior two-accusative naming frame.

example_models.translation: He commanded the man to go.
example_models.note: The infinitive gān makes this the commanding frame, despite the same hēt spelling as the naming example.
